passages.sourceText: Begin with the graph at rest. Price, [$P$](kp-ref:price-axis-inline), is vertical and quantity, $Q$, is horizontal. The blue supply schedule, $S$, rises while the red demand schedule, $D_0$, falls.
Before continuing, hold blue $S$ fixed and watch red demand. The two schedules meet at $E_0=(6,8)$. This point is equilibrium because buyers and sellers choose the same quantity at the same price.
Red demand has shifted from $D_0$ to $D_1$ while blue $S$ stayed fixed. Its intersection with supply moved as well.

The curves now meet at $E_1=(8,10)$, above and to the right of $E_0$. Both equilibrium price and equilibrium quantity are higher. Next, ignore red demand and watch the equilibrium move along blue $S$.
The trace has moved from $E_0$ to $E_1$ along blue $S$ without changing the supply curve itself.
Sellers supply more because the higher clearing price selects a new point on unchanged $S$. Quantity supplied moved; the supply curve did not shift.
